passage:
There was always one empty seat in the front row of Room 305. No one sat there because it was too close to the teacher's desk. Most students wanted to sit farther back.
One day, a new student named Jason came into the classroom. He looked around and sat in the empty seat. Some students smiled because they thought he did not know why the seat was empty.
But Jason liked it there. He could hear the teacher clearly, see the board well, and ask questions easily. After a few weeks, his grades improved quickly.
Soon, other students began to think differently about the front row. The empty seat was no longer a bad place. It was just a place no one had tried.
